subject: Discovery Recap — Observability & Evals
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava@orbitai.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos@orbitai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap — Observability & Evals

Hi Ava / Carlos,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

High-level pain points you called out:
- Lack of reliable model-level regression alerts and guardrails as you scale evaluations across teams.
- Limited visibility into per-request latency/cost tradeoffs for different model variants and quantization profiles.
- Difficulty reproducing eval regressions (no golden prompt sets with stable baselines).

Current stack you shared:
- Hosting: AWS EKS + internal autoscaling (K8s)
- Observability: Datadog for infra + Sentry for app errors
- Evals: in-house scripts (Python + Jupyter), results in CSVs stored on S3

Success criteria you mentioned:
1) Detect and alert on quality regressions within a 24-hour window tied to a golden prompt set.
2) Per-route dashboards showing latency, cost-per-token, and % of responses that hit fallback.
3) Tracing hooks to link inference requests to upstream user context and downstream logs.

Actions / next steps (proposed):
- I will share a short observability & evals deck + a golden-prompt template (attached).  
- We can spin up a 2-week eval with Redwood: we’ll provide an eval runner + dashboard for one critical route.
- Technical Qs for your infra team (cc’ing Rishi & Priyom): how do you currently ship request-scoped tracing headers?

Attachments: redwood-observability-deck.pdf (attachment), golden-prompt-sets.csv (attachment), evals-template.xlsx (attachment)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a technical sync next week once I hear from Rishi/ Priyom.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
From: Ava Reynolds <ava@orbitai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos@orbitai.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap — Observability & Evals

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the thorough recap — this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and answers:

- Priority: our top priority is the regression detection + golden prompts for our fraud detection assistant. If we can detect a drift or quality regression automatically and tie it back to a release or model change, that will unblock QA.
- Tracing: we propagate a request-id header through our services; we don’t currently attach user context to model requests (we can add a lightweight context header).
- Dashboards: Datadog is our primary dashboard; we’d prefer a solution that either pushes metrics into Datadog or exposes a stable set of metrics we can ingest.
- Evals: we currently run nightly batch evals; they’re brittle and take too long — surprising to hear Redwood can run an eval runner against a pinned model version.

Quick answers to your Qs for infra: we can add the tracing header; I’ll loop in infra if Rishi needs deeper access.

Next steps from our side:
1) Please send the deck and templates (got them — will review).
2) Schedule the technical sync (Rishi and infra will join).
3) Pricing/PO: Carlos will lead procurement conversations after we validate the eval workflow.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the tech sync.

Best,
Ava Reynolds
Head of ML Platform | OrbitAI
ava@orbitai.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery Recap — Observability & Evals

FYI — forwarding OrbitAI’s quick responses. Can you help with the two technical Qs below before I lock the tech sync?

Technical points to confirm:
- Tracing hooks: we support both sending a request-id plus optional user-context header (X-User-ID). We can provide a lightweight lib that adds these headers and a short snippet to correlate in Datadog. Are there any security constraints on sending user identifiers?
- Eval runner: to run their nightly evals in a more reproducible way we’ll provide a containerized runner that pins model SHA/quant config and uploads metrics to our dashboard — do we need to whitelist any of their IPs or VPC endpoints to reach the runner?

OrbitAI folks: I’ll hold off on scheduling the sync until Rishi confirms the tracing approach + network needs.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Ava / Carlos — quick follow-up with answers and proposed schedule.

Answers from our infra/product team (copied):
- Tracing & user context: Rishi confirmed we support a request-id header plus an optional X-User-ID. We’ll provide a 2-file helper (Node + Python) that attaches both headers and a short Datadog example showing how to correlate traces with model request metrics. No PII needs to be sent; X-User-ID can be an internal hashed id if you prefer.
- Network/runner access: Priyom confirmed the eval runner is outbound-only from Redwood and does not require whitelisting inbound IPs. We will provide a small Docker image that runs in your environment or in ours. If you want the runner inside your VPC, we support a private deployment option — we can scope that after the eval.

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- Technical sync (30m): Thu, Mar 26 at 10:00am PT — goal: walk through tracing snippet and confirm the golden prompt seed set. (If that time works I’ll send calendar invite).
- Eval kickoff: Week of Mar 30 — Redwood will run an initial 2-week eval against the fraud assistant route. We’ll provide dashboards (Datadog export + Redwood console link) and an initial regression alert policy (example attached).
- Success criteria for pilot: 24-hour regression alerting on golden prompts, dashboard showing latency/cost by model variant, reproducible evals via pinned runner.

Attachments: redwood-observability-deck.pdf, golden-prompt-sets.csv, evals-template.xlsx

Optional: I’ve also added a short example of a regression alert policy in the deck and a sample Datadog query you can paste into your account.

If that looks good I’ll: 1) send the calendar invite for Thu, 3/26 10am PT, 2) create a HubSpot deal and add the eval playbook.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
